overview: The Medford City Council approved a common victualler license for a non-profit coffee cart at the public library and passed resolutions concerning street landscaping, state highway maintenance schedules, park dog safety, and city website updates. A resident also addressed the council regarding park upkeep and municipal staffing during public participation.

items.title: Common Victualler License for Chapters Coffee Carts
items.summary: The council approved a common victualler license application for Chapters Coffee Carts Corporation to operate at the Medford Public Library.

items.title: Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: The council approved the meeting records from May 24, 2022, and accepted a Committee of the Whole report regarding pre-budget priorities.

items.title: Eversource Project Update Request
items.summary: The council considered a resolution requesting an update from Eversource and city officials on ongoing work at Mystic Avenue and Winthrop Street.

items.title: Street Bump-Out Maintenance and Adopt-A-Site Program
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting cleanup of street bump-outs and center islands, as well as a status report on the city's Adopt-A-Site program.

items.title: State Maintenance Schedules for Route 93 Ramps and Rotaries
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting MassDOT to mow grass along Route 93 ramps and rotaries, along with maintenance schedules from MassDOT and DCR.

items.title: Tufts Park Off-Leash Dog Safety Concerns
items.summary: The council approved a resolution requesting an administrative report on off-leash dog safety at Tufts Park and exploring a temporary pilot fence at the former pool site.

items.title: City Website COVID-19 Information Update
items.summary: The council approved a resolution asking the administration to update COVID-19 information on the city website, alongside requests for updates on IT security and hiring.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Resident Nate Merritt spoke regarding park maintenance, off-leash dog safety, and code enforcement staffing, prompting discussion among councilors about budget priorities.
